content.title: Gerry McIlroy, Father Of Rory, Has Found His Home At Seminole
content.text: Masters Triumph Casts Woods In Yet Another New Light Ron Green Jr. After all these years – the highs, the lows, the smiles, the limps and even the mock turtlenecks – you’d think we’d have seen everything from Tiger Woods.But it’s hard not to see him differently – again.The next time Woods tees it up, mostly likely in the PGA Championship two weeks from now after his decision to bypass the Wells Fargo Championship this week, it will be different. His majesty has not just been restored, it has been recast with an even deeper appreciation of his achievements.What he did in winning the Masters earlier this month is like The Beatles having gotten back together in the early ’90s and producing an album every bit as good as Revolver or Abbey Road.It’s like Michael Jordan coming out of a three-year retirement to lead the Washington Wizards to … never mind. That one didn’t work out so well.For two decades, we’ve compared Woods to Jack Nicklaus and now he’s gone all Ben Hogan on us, not just making a comeback but winning his 15th major, restarting multiple countdowns that lead to Olympus.Woods himself said he hasn’t fully comprehended his achievement. He spent the past two weeks mostly hanging out at home in South Florida, taking his kids to school and decompressing.“I haven’t come to grips with what I accomplished. It’s very similar to 1997. That took years to understand what I accomplished. I don’t think this one will settle in for quite a while.”Tiger WoodsOnce in a while, Woods told GolfTV (with whom he has a contract to provide exclusive content), he finds himself on his couch and looking over to see the green jacket.“I haven’t come to grips with what I accomplished,” Woods said in the interview. “It’s very similar to 1997. That took years to understand what I accomplished. I don’t think this one will settle in for quite a while.”The first 14 majors on Tiger’s résumé we all knew he could win.This one, this was more hope than belief. His Tour Championship victory last fall was inspiring, a demonstration that Woods could still do this.But winning the Masters, beating Dustin Johnson and Brooks Koepka and all the others who had moved into the void his departure had created, well, that was dream chasing.Then he did it.On the final nine holes at Augusta National, he became Tiger Woods again.Just like he used to be. Only different.Better in some ways because of where he’d been, what he’d been through and how he came out on the other side, arms spread, pulling his kids into a hug the world felt. Tiger Woods embraces his son after his Masters victory, as his mother, his daughter and his girlfriend look on. He’s not ready to stop – Woods needs one win to equal Sam Snead’s PGA Tour record of 82 victories and there are three more majors to tie Nicklaus – but if he never wins another tournament, what he did winning the Masters will shine like a Christmas tree on a dark night.It’s not entirely surprising that Woods decided to skip playing at Quail Hollow, one of the places he’s typically played through the years. Listening to him in the one interview he’s given since his victory, it was apparent he was still gearing down rather than gearing up.“I want to enjoy this,” Woods said. “But also down in the back of my mind thinking, ‘You know what, I have another major in about a month.’ The prep starts. I can mentally prep for this.“I don’t really want to do too much right now. I haven’t gotten to the point where I’m willing to put in the hours yet and do the dirty stuff to get the body ready, to put in all the hours of hitting golf balls and putting. I’m doing all the visual stuff, but I haven’t put in the physical work yet. But it’s probably coming this (past) weekend.''Woods has made no secret of his intention to trim his schedule this year and it’s possible he will make just 10 starts through the Open Championship in July. Assuming he doesn’t play the AT&T Byron Nelson next week, Woods will play the PGA Championship, most likely the Memorial Tournament, the U.S. Open and the Open Championship.That’s 10 events before a three-event run in the FedEx Cup playoffs. There is some thought that Woods will add an event in the summer, perhaps the new 3M Open in Minneapolis two weeks before the Open Championship, but that’s idle speculation right now.When Woods gets to rugged Bethpage Black, where he won the 2002 U.S. Open, he will be the favorite entering the PGA Championship, not just emotionally, but for all the right reasons.There is an art to winning and he is the ultimate artist. Some tried to suggest that Woods’ Masters victory was the result of other players falling back on Sunday, leaving him with the lead when it was over.That’s how Nicklaus often won. He talked about that, almost bragged about how he let others lose so he could win. On the closing holes at Augusta National, Woods gave a demonstration of course management and execution under the most demanding conditions. It was like a lecture from Einstein – without the equations.As Friday ticked away in Charlotte, N.C., there was an urgency among the locals about whether Woods would play at Quail Hollow. They wanted to see him again, in the flesh, knowing what he’d accomplished at Augusta National.When it became evident the Wells Fargo Championship will go on without him – it’s still stacked with Rory McIlroy, Justin Rose, Rickie Fowler, Jason Day, Phil Mickelson and others – it was a letdown.The people wanted more Tiger.For the new Tiger, less is more.E-Mail Ron
